title: Mequon-Thiensville district launches long-range facilities planning process
text:
Schools
Mequon-Thiensville district launches long-range facilities planning process
MTSD has begun a long-range facilities master planning process covering classroom capacity, maintenance and athletics, the district said.
The Mequon-Thiensville School District has launched a long-range facilities master planning process, according to the district's October Momentum family newsletter, posted Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026.
The planning process covers four areas, the district said. One focus is instructional spaces and capacity, which includes assessing how classrooms and shared spaces support modern teaching practices and evaluating building capacity and section needs, such as spatial capacity at Oriole Lane, using updated demographic data.
A second area is capital maintenance, with the district working to create a predictable 10-year maintenance plan covering building mechanical systems such as HVAC, electrical and plumbing, along with structural envelopes and safety infrastructure, according to the newsletter.
The district also plans to model adaptable financial scenarios intended to ensure operational stability across school environments as part of a fiscal sustainability component, and to integrate high school athletic facility planning into the districtwide facility schedule under an athletic and campus facilities component, the district said.
The same newsletter included results from the district's 2026 September Family Survey. MTSD achieved an overall Net Promoter Score of 55, matching last year's rating, with elementary families accounting for 60% of all responses, according to the district. The survey also found that 86% of new families enrolled because of the district's academic reputation, 93% of respondents reported their children feel safe at school, 88% felt well-prepared and welcomed before the first day of school, and 85% of families transitioning to new buildings felt orientation eased the move, the district said.
The newsletter also noted that 2027-28 school year calendars have been approved.
Source: Donges Bay Elementary School, https://donges-bay.mtsd.k12.wi.us/index.php?pageID=smartSiteFeed&psqFeed=true&articleID=94611391
